ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle JPL, with P at the lower left, L at the lower right, and J above. Point Q is on side JP, point M is on side PL, and point S is inside the triangle. In the figure, there is a line segment from P to S, and 28° is marked at P; this angle lies between PM (along the direction of the base PL) and PS. Reasoning: The problem states that S is the incenter of triangle JPL, so the line segment PS from vertex P to S is the angle bisector of the vertex angle ∠JPL. Since Q is on JP and M is on PL, ∠MPQ is the entire angle at vertex P formed by PM and PQ. The marked 28° in the figure is half of it, namely ∠MPS = 28°, so ∠MPQ = 2 × 28° = 56°.
